help.search.title: Searching the help
body: Type one or more words: a topic is listed when its title or text has **every** word. Case and accents don't matter, and words in the title rank first.
With nothing typed, every topic is listed from A to Z. Every round **?** in the app opens the topic for the thing next to it.

app.overview.title: How HandBrake Queue works
body: HandBrake Queue converts videos that are already on the server, using HandBrakeCLI with presets exported from the HandBrake desktop app. Nothing is uploaded or downloaded.
### The usual workflow
1. Upload a [preset](#presets) exported from HandBrake.
1. In **Convert**, drag files or folders from [Sources](#convert.sources) into the [Queue](#convert.queue).
1. Press **Start**: see [Starting and stopping the queue](#queue.state).
1. Each converted file is [checked](#verify.overview) for errors, missing audio or subtitles and the right length.
1. In **Rename**, give the converted files clean names: see [Renaming files](#rename.overview).
Optionally, join several converted files into one (e.g. a film split in two parts) in **Merge**: see [Merging files](#merge.overview).
Source files are never changed or deleted, so downloads can keep seeding.

convert.sources.title: Sources
body: The folders and video files under the **Sources folder** set in [Settings](#settings.folders). Only folders and video files are listed (see [Adding folders](#settings.adding) for the extensions).
- **Double-click** a folder to open it, or a file to add it to the queue.
- **Drag** files or folders onto the Queue to add them. Ctrl-click and Shift-click select several; the checkbox at the top selects everything.
- **Add to queue** adds what is selected.
- Adding a folder adds every video inside it, sub-folders included. Files already queued are skipped, and so are files already converted unless you turned that off.
Badges show what happened to each file: **Queued**, **Converting**, **Converted**, **Failed**. On folders they count the files inside.
Adding files never starts converting: press **Start** when you are ready ([why](#queue.state)).

convert.queue.title: Queue
body: Every file to convert is a **job**. Jobs run one at a time, top to bottom.
- **Preset**: the [preset](#presets) used for the files you add next. A queued job's preset can be changed in its details.
- **Add**: put new files **at the end** of the queue or **next**, before the other waiting jobs.
- **Drag** a queued job by its handle (⋮⋮) to change the order, or use **Move to top**.

- The filters show all jobs, the active ones, the converted ones or the failed and cancelled ones. **Rename these** (under Converted) opens their files in the Rename view, **Merge these** in the Merge view.
- **Clear finished** removes converted, failed and cancelled jobs from the list. Files are not touched.
Click a job to see its [details](#job.details).

queue.state.title: Starting and stopping the queue
body: The queue **never starts by itself**: adding or dropping files only puts them in the list. Press **Start** to begin converting.
- While it runs, files you add join the run.
- When the last job is done the queue stops again, so the next files you add wait for **Start**.
- **Stop after current** lets the job being converted finish, then stops. To stop at once, pause or cancel that job.
- If the server restarts during a run, the run continues after the restart. The job that was converting starts again from 0%, because HandBrake cannot resume an encode halfway.

job.statuses.title: Job statuses
body: - **Queued**: waiting for its turn.
- **Scanning**: HandBrake is reading the source before converting.
- **Converting**: encoding, with progress, speed (frames per second) and time left.
- **Finishing**: HandBrake is writing the end of the file.
- **Checking**: the converted file is being [checked](#verify.overview).
- **Paused**: stopped where it was; **Resume** continues.
- **Converted**: done. A second badge shows the result of the check: **Checked**, **Check warnings** or **Check failed**.
- **Failed**: HandBrake stopped with an error; the details show why and the log has more.
- **Cancelled**: you cancelled it.

job.actions.title: Job actions
body: - **Pause / Resume**: freezes the conversion (or the check) and continues it later. Restarting the server while paused starts the conversion again from 0%.

- **Cancel**: stops the conversion and deletes the half-written file. On a queued job it only marks it cancelled. While the file is being checked, **Skip check** keeps the converted file and skips the rest of the check.
- **Move to top**: converts this queued job next.
- **Retry**: puts a failed or cancelled job back in the queue.
- **Convert again**: a new job for the same source. The new file gets a suffix such as `name (1).mkv`, so the first one is kept. In the details you can choose another preset.
- **Rename**: opens the converted file in the [Rename view](#rename.overview).
- **Check again**: runs the [check](#verify.overview) on a converted file again.
- **Remove**: takes the job off the list. Files are never deleted.

job.details.title: Job details
body: Everything about one job: [progress](#job.statuses), the [check](#verify.results), [files](#job.files), preset, [source](#job.source), [timing](#job.timing) and the [HandBrake log](#job.log). The buttons at the top are the [job actions](#job.actions).
The details follow the job live while it converts. Close them with ✕ or Escape.

job.files.title: Source and output files
body: - **Source**: the file being converted. It is never changed.

- **Output**: where the converted file goes, under the **Target folder** in the layout chosen in [Settings](#settings.layout). While the job is queued you can **edit** it (it must stay inside the target folder).
- If a file with that name already exists when the job starts, the new file gets a suffix: `name (1).mkv`. Nothing is overwritten.
- While converting, the output is written as `name.mkv.part` and renamed when HandBrake finishes, so media servers never pick up half-written files.
- **Sizes** compares the source with the output.

job.source.title: Source details
body: What HandBrake found in the source when the job was added: length, video format and size, frame rate, and the audio and subtitle tracks with their languages.
The [preset](#presets) decides which of these tracks go into the output. The [check](#verify.overview) compares the output with what HandBrake meant to write.

job.timing.title: Timing
body: When the job was added, started and finished, how long encoding took (pauses not counted) and the average speed in frames per second. **Attempts** counts how many times it was started, e.g. after a retry or a restart.

job.log.title: HandBrake log
body: Everything HandBrakeCLI printed while converting: the settings it used, the tracks it picked, warnings and errors. It updates live while the job runs.

When a job fails, the error shown in its details comes from the last error lines of this log. The [check](#verify.overview) also reads it, to know which audio and subtitle tracks HandBrake wrote and whether it found errors in the source.

verify.overview.title: Checking converted files
body: After each successful conversion the output is checked before the job is marked converted. The job shows **Checking** meanwhile, and the next job waits.
### What is checked
- **Readable**: the file opens and has a video stream.

- **Length matches the source**: where the video really ends, measured by reading the whole file. A file cut short can still claim the full length in its metadata, so that alone isn't trusted. Up to 2 seconds (or 0.5%) of difference is fine, up to 10 seconds (or 2%) is a warning, more is an error.
- **Audio tracks**: the file has every audio track HandBrake wrote (from the [log](#job.log)), and each one lasts as long as the video.

- **Subtitle tracks**: the file has every subtitle track HandBrake passed through. Subtitles burned into the picture are part of the video. A track with no lines (e.g. forced subtitles in an episode without any) is shown but is not a problem.
- **Full decode**: every video and audio frame is decoded to find damaged data. It takes about 1–2 minutes for a 45-minute episode.
- **Source**: if HandBrake found decoding errors in the source, the damage may be visible in the output too (a warning).
Choose **Full**, **Quick** (everything except the full decode) or **Off** in [Settings](#settings.encoding).

verify.results.title: Check results
body: - **Checked** (green): every check passed.
- **Check warnings** (amber): something to look at, e.g. errors in the source or a few seconds of difference in length. The file is usually fine.
- **Check failed** (red): the file is probably broken: too short, a missing or short audio track, or many decoding errors. Use **Convert again**, or try another source.
- **Not checked**: the check was skipped, stopped by a restart, or turned off.
Each line in the job details says what was found. **Check again** repeats the check, e.g. after copying the file back.
Files that fail the check are never [renamed automatically](#rename.auto).

presets.title: Presets
body: A preset holds every conversion setting: video encoder and quality, size, frame rate, audio and subtitle tracks, container. Presets are made in the HandBrake desktop app and uploaded here.
1. In HandBrake: **Presets** → select your preset → **Export**.
1. Here: drop the `.json` file in **Presets**, or choose it.
- A file can hold several presets, also inside folders: each one is added.
- Uploading a preset with the same name again replaces the old one.
- The **default** preset (★) is used when you add files, unless you choose another one in the Queue.
- Each job keeps a copy of its preset, so changing or deleting a preset never changes jobs already in the queue.

The encoder always comes from the preset. Hardware encoders (`qsv_h264`, `qsv_h265`) only work on Intel CPUs from 11th generation on; the encoders available on this server are listed in Settings → About.

settings.folders.title: Sources and target folders
body: Folders on the server (not on your computer). NAS shares mounted on the server work too.
- **Sources folder**: where the files to convert are. The Sources panel can't go above it.
- **Target folder**: where converted files are written. The Rename view works only here.
Both must exist, and the target cannot be inside the sources folder. In Docker they must be inside the folder mounted into the container (`MEDIA_DIR`, usually `/mnt`).

settings.layout.title: Output folder layout
body: Where under the target folder each converted file goes:
- **Source folder name**: `target/Show.S01/episode.mkv`, using only the name of the folder the source is in. Good for season folders.
- **Full source path**: `target/Completed/Show.S01/episode.mkv`, the whole path below the sources folder.
- **All in the target folder**: `target/episode.mkv`.
If the file already exists, the new one gets a suffix (`episode (1).mkv`). The layout applies to files added after the change; queued jobs keep their output path.

settings.adding.title: Adding folders
body: - **Include sub-folders**: adding a folder also adds the videos in its sub-folders.
- **Skip files that were already converted**: a file with a converted job is not added again. Use **Convert again** on its job to redo one.
- **Video file extensions**: which files count as videos, separated by commas.
- **Skip files and folders containing these words**: whole words, any case, e.g. `sample` skips `show-sample.mkv` and a `Sample` folder but not `samples.mkv`.

settings.encoding.title: Encoding settings
body: - **CPU priority**: how politely conversions share the CPU with other services on the server (Linux `nice`, 0–19). Higher is gentler and slower only when the server is busy.

- **Check after conversion**: **Full** (every check, with a complete decode), **Quick** (lengths, tracks and readability without decoding) or **Off**. See [Checking converted files](#verify.overview).

settings.renaming.title: Renaming settings
body: - **Rename files automatically after conversion**: off by default. See [Automatic renaming](#rename.auto).
- **Rule set for automatic renaming**: which [rule set](#rename.rules) is used.
- **Separator**: when the new name is taken, a number is added after it: with `_` you get `name_1.mkv`, `name_2.mkv`.

rename.overview.title: Renaming files
body: Downloaded files have names like `The.Rookie.6x01.Title.ITA.ENG.1080p.NFRip.AAC.x265-Pir8`. The Rename view turns them into `The Rookie S06e01 - Title`, using [rule sets](#rename.rules).
1. On the left, browse the **target folder** and drag converted files or folders to the rename list (or use **Rename** on a converted job).
1. Pick the **Rules**. The built-in **Auto** recognises both TV episodes and movies.
1. Look at the [preview](#rename.preview): fix any name by hand, and type a [show name](#rename.showName) where none was found.
1. Press **Rename**. Every batch can be undone from [History](#rename.history).
Only files in the target folder can be renamed, never the sources (downloads may still be seeding).

rename.preview.title: Rename preview
body: Each row shows the current name (small, grey) and the new name. Nothing changes on disk until you press **Rename**.
- **Edit** any new name by typing in it (Enter to confirm, Escape to cancel). An edited row is blue; **undo edit** goes back to the rules' name.
- **Ticks** choose which rows are renamed. Rows with a warning start unticked: check them and tick them when they look right.
- **Warnings** explain what the rules couldn't find, e.g. no episode number, no year, or no show name.
- **TV · S06e01** or **Movie · 2024** shows what was recognised; **no change** means the name is already right.
- If two files would get the same name, or the name is taken by another file in the folder, a number is added: `name_1.mkv` (see [Renaming settings](#settings.renaming)).
Files in different folders are grouped under their folder.

rename.showName.title: Show name
body: Some files don't have the show name before the episode number, e.g. `S04E07 Reacher Tutti Con Sampson (2026)…`. Type the show name (`Reacher`) and the rows get `Reacher S04e07 - Tutti Con Sampson`; the name is also taken out of the episode title.
- **only where missing** (default): only rows where no show name was found get it. Other shows in the same list keep theirs.
- **for all rows**: every TV row gets this show name, e.g. to shorten a long one or to add a year for a remake: `Silo (2023)`.

rename.rules.title: Rename rule sets
body: A rule set is a list of [steps](#rename.steps) applied in order to each file name (without its extension).
- **Built-in** rule sets (**Auto**, **TV series**, **Movies**) can't be changed: use **Duplicate** to make an editable copy.
- **New** starts a rule set with the [Recognise episode / movie](#rename.smart) step.

- **Import** reads Advanced Renamer presets (`.aren`) as well as rule sets exported from here. Every Advanced Renamer method used for names (replace, remove pattern, remove, add, move, trim, case) becomes a step.
- **Export** (download icon) saves the rule set as a `.json` file, e.g. to copy it to another server.
- Changes are kept only after **Save**; [Try it](#rename.tryIt) shows the result before saving.

rename.steps.title: Rename steps
body: Steps run top to bottom; untick one to switch it off without deleting it. Click a step to edit it.
- **Recognise episode / movie**: builds the whole name from a template. See [Recognise episode / movie](#rename.smart).
- **Remove release tags**: cuts the name at the first tag such as `1080p`, `WEB-DL`, `x265` or `ITA`.
- **Replace**: finds text and replaces it: all, first or last occurrence, matching case or not. With **Regular expression**, `$1`, `$2`… insert the groups found.
- **Remove pattern**: deletes what matches, e.g. `(720p).*$` deletes from `720p` to the end.
- **Remove everything after text**: e.g. after `)`.
- **Remove characters / Add text / Move characters**: work on positions, like Advanced Renamer. Positions change with each file name, so pattern steps are usually safer.
- **Trim characters**: removes the listed characters from both ends.
- **Change case**: Title Case, UPPER, lower or Sentence case.
- **Fix apostrophes**: `L Uomo` → `L'Uomo`, `Dell Oca` → `Dell'Oca`, `Wouldn T` → `Wouldn't`.
- **Collapse spaces**: several spaces become one.
Characters that file names can't contain (`/ \ : * ? " < > |`) are removed or replaced at the end; `:` becomes ` -`.

rename.smart.title: Recognise episode / movie
body: Reads the parts of a release name and builds a clean one.
- **TV**: finds `S01E02`, `S01E01E02` or `1x02`. The show is the text before it, the episode title the text after it, up to the first release tag.
- **Movie**: finds the year (`2024` or `(2024)`); the title is the text before it.
- **Type**: **Auto** treats a name with an episode number as TV and anything else as a movie.
### Templates

`{show}`, `{season}`, `{episode}`, `{title}` and `{year}` are replaced by what was found; season and episode get two digits. A part in `[ ]` disappears when a field inside it is empty: `{show} S{season}e{episode}[ - {title}]` gives `Lanterns S01e01` when there is no episode title.
### Options
- **Title Case words**: capitalises each word, keeping capitals already there (`McLaren`, `INXS`).
- **Fix apostrophes**: `L Osservatore` → `L'Osservatore`.
- **Keep the year in the show name**: `East of Eden 2026 S01E01` becomes `East Of Eden (2026) S01e01`. Off by default; useful for remakes.
- **Extra release tags**: more words that mark the start of the release information.

rename.tryIt.title: Try it
body: Shows what the rule set being edited does to some names, before saving. It starts with the names in your rename list (or a few examples); type or paste any names, one per line.
The **Show name** box works like the one in the [Rename view](#rename.showName).

rename.history.title: Rename history
body: Every batch of renames, newest first, including automatic ones. Click a batch to see each old and new name.
**Undo** gives the files their old names back. A file is skipped if it was deleted or moved since, or if its old name is in use again.

rename.auto.title: Automatic renaming
body: When **Rename files automatically after conversion** is on (Settings → Renaming), each converted file is renamed with the chosen rule set right after its [check](#verify.overview).

To stay safe, a file is renamed only when the rules recognise it **without warnings**. Otherwise the job shows **Needs rename** and you finish it in the [Rename view](#rename.overview). Files that fail the check are not renamed.
Automatic renames appear in [History](#rename.history) and can be undone.

merge.overview.title: Merging files
body: Joins converted files into one MKV, one after the other, for example a film or a concert split into discs or parts. The chapters of every part are kept.
1. On the left, browse the **target folder** and drag the parts (or the folder holding them) to the merge list. Under **Converted** in the queue, **Merge these** does the same.
1. Put the parts [in order](#merge.parts).
1. Read the [compatibility check](#merge.compat): parts that cannot be joined are explained there.
1. Choose the [name and chapters](#merge.options) of the merged file and press **Merge**.

Merging copies the video, audio and subtitles as they are, without converting again, so it takes about as long as copying the files. The merged file is then [checked](#verify.overview) like a conversion: its length must be the parts added together, with the same audio and subtitle tracks as part 1.
Merges run one at a time, alongside conversions. Progress and results are under [Recent merges](#merge.history). The parts are kept unless you choose to delete them.

merge.parts.title: Parts and their order
body: The merged file plays the parts top to bottom. A dropped folder adds its video files in name order (`Disc 1`, `Disc 2`, … `Disc 10`).
- **Drag** a part by its handle, or use the arrows, to change the order.
- ✕ takes a part out of the list (the file is not touched).
Each row shows the part’s length, chapters, audio languages, subtitle tracks, picture size and file size, read from the file.

merge.compat.title: Can the parts be joined?
body: Joining files only works when every part has the **same tracks in the same order**. The easiest way is to convert all parts with the same preset.
### Problems that stop the merge (red)
- A different number of video, audio or subtitle tracks, e.g. one part with Italian and English audio and another with Italian only.
- A track in a different format (e.g. AAC in one part, AC-3 in another), or audio with different channels or sample rate.
### Warnings (amber): the merge can go ahead
- A different picture size, or video encoded with slightly different settings (e.g. a different crop). Most players handle it; some may glitch for a moment where the parts join, so check the joins.
- A track in another language: the merged track keeps part 1’s language.

merge.chapters.title: Chapters of the merged file
body: - **Keep each part’s chapters** (default): every chapter keeps its place, moved to where its part starts in the merged file. HandBrake’s generic names (`Chapter 1`, `Chapter 2`…) are renumbered across the whole file; chapters with their own names keep them. A part without chapters gets one chapter named after the file.
- **One chapter per part**: one chapter at the start of each part, named after its file (dots and underscores become spaces).
Open **chapters in the merged file** under the options to see the list before merging.

merge.options.title: Name and options of the merged file
body: - **Name**: suggested from what the parts’ names have in common (`Live Aid - Disc 1`, `Live Aid - Disc 2` → `Live Aid`). The file is always `.mkv`.
- The merged file goes in the **folder of part 1**. If the name is taken, a number is added (`Live Aid_1.mkv`, see [Renaming settings](#settings.renaming)). Nothing is overwritten.
- **Chapters**: see [Chapters of the merged file](#merge.chapters).

- **Delete the parts after a successful merge**: off by default. The parts are deleted only if the merge worked and the [check](#verify.overview) did not fail; if checking is off, they are deleted after the merge. This cannot be undone.
While merging, the file is written as `name.mkv.part` and renamed at the end, so media servers never see a half-written file.

merge.history.title: Recent merges
body: Each merge with its status: **Waiting**, **Reading parts**, **Merging** (with progress), **Checking**, **Merged**, **Failed** or **Cancelled**. A merged file also shows its [check result](#verify.results).
Click a merge to see the output, the parts, any warnings from mkvmerge and the check details.
- ■ cancels a waiting or running merge; the half-written file is deleted and the parts are kept.
- 🗑 removes a finished merge from the list. Files are not touched.
